zotero.abstractNote: Similarity-based retrieval systems, such as those powered by CLIP, are increasingly used to search through large-scale image and text databases. These systems rely on the assumption that the similarity score between a query and a retrieved item is a reliable indicator of relevance. In this paper, we show that this assumption is often violated by 'half-truths'—retrieved items that are partially relevant but misleading. We demonstrate that these half-truths can significantly degrade the performance of similarity-based retrieval systems, and we propose a simple yet effective method to mitigate this issue.
